name: Dandelion
description: Radical dispersal and deep resource intelligence. Parachute-geometry seeds achieve wind-optimized flight via a separated vortex ring — a fluid dynamics structure unknown in engineering until studied in dandelion pappus. Taproots mine minerals from depths inaccessible to shallow-rooted competitors. Rapid lifecycle cycling enables colonization of disturbed ground before other species arrive.

core_attributes.pattern: wind-optimized dispersal, deep taproot mineral access, rapid lifecycle cycling

scope.definition: Dispersal efficiency of dandelion pappus aerofoil — fraction of seeds achieving minimum 1 km dispersal distance from parent plant under moderate breeze (2-4 m/s), measured by stable vortex ring formation.

evidence.source: Cummins et al. (2018) 'A separated vortex ring underlies the flight of the dandelion', Nature 562:414-418.
cross_domain_examples: dandelion pappus achieves 100 km dispersal range in controlled airflow — far exceeding most seed wings
separated vortex ring (wake-captured) flight mode 4× more efficient than equivalent solid parachute
sycamore samara: spinning autorotation for controlled descent — parallel wind-dispersal morphology optimization

scope.falsifiability: If pappus seeds in wind-tunnel tests show no stable vortex formation and descent rates comparable to non-porous equivalents, the vortex-ring flight model is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: Dispersal efficiency depends on humidity — wet conditions cause pappus collapse. Maximum dispersal achieved at 30-40% relative humidity. Seed:pappus mass ratio optimized for vortex stability.
